    Latest Update: A streaming pipeline turned a data lake bill into an API bill

    📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (977 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dev

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Originally published on the Cloud ex Machina engineering blog.
    • It has been revealed that A data lake bucket held less than a terabyte and cost about $5 a day.
    • The two pipelines are Lakeflow Declarative Pipelines on Databricks, formerly Delta Live Tables, running in continuous mode, so they "process new data as it arrives" and never stop.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Originally published on the Cloud ex Machina engineering blog.

    It has been revealed that A data lake bucket held less than a terabyte and cost about $5 a day. On the day two new Databricks streaming pipelines went live, its cost rose to almost $19 a day, and S3 request costs made up 97% of it. The pipelines worked as written, the tables stayed fresh, and every dashboard stayed green. Two configuration defaults drove the extra cost, and the signal sat on the cloud bill, far from the pipeline code and its tests. A few lines of configuration fixed it, for about $5,000 a year. This post opens Feedback loops from the FinOps trenches, our series on runtime signals that point back at the code that caused them.

    The two pipelines are Lakeflow Declarative Pipelines on Databricks, formerly Delta Live Tables, running in continuous mode, so they "process new data as it arrives" and never stop. Their source changes rarely. Every 35 to 70 seconds, each pipeline checked for new data, found none, and wrote down that it had found none. One of the two tables had never received a row.

    Each of those notes costs requests. A streaming job records its progress in a streaming checkpoint, and it splits its state into one folder per shuffle partition. Spark's spark.sql.shuffle.partitions defaults to 200, and the checkpoint we looked at had 201 state folders. Each empty micro-batch listed and wrote files across all of them.

    In the 32 days after go-live, the bucket averaged:.

    Recent findings suggest that S3 bills lists and writes at the same $0.005 per thousand, more than twelve times the price of a read. The bucket's own bill shows it: 76.2 million list requests cost $380.98 in one month, while storage stayed under $1 a day.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • It has been revealed that affiliate marketing is a way to make money by promoting the products and services of other people and companies.
    • An affiliate program is a package of information you create for your product, which is then made available to potential publishers.
    • Industry observers note that affiliate networks connect publishers to advertisers.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    It has been revealed that affiliate marketing is a way to make money by promoting the products and services of other people and companies. You don't need to create your product or service, just promote existing ones. That's why it's so easy to get started with affiliate marketing. You can even get started with no budget at all!

    An affiliate program is a package of information you create for your product, which is then made available to potential publishers. The program will typically include details about the product and its retail value, commission levels, and promotional materials. Many affiliate programs are managed via an affiliate network like ShareASale, which acts as a platform to connect publishers and advertisers, but it is also possible to offer your program directly.

    Industry observers note that affiliate networks connect publishers to advertisers. Affiliate networks make money by charging fees to the merchants who advertise with them; these merchants are known as advertisers. The percentage of each sale that the advertiser pays is negotiated between the merchant and the affiliate network.

    Dropshipping is a method of selling that allows you to run an online store without having to stock products. You advertise the products as if you owned them, but when someone makes an order, you create a duplicate order with the distributor at a reduced price. The distributor takes care of the post and packaging on your behalf. As affiliate marketing is based on referrals and this type of drop shipping requires no investment in inventory when a customer buys through the affiliate link, no money exchanges hands.

    Performance marketing is a method of marketing that pays for performance, like when a sale is made or an ad is clicked This can include methods like PPC (pay-per-click) or display advertising. Affiliate marketing is one form of performance marketing where commissions are paid out to affiliates on a performance basis when they click on their affiliate link and make a purchase or action.

    Sources indicate that smartphones are essentially miniature computers, so publishers can display the same websites and offers that are available on a PC. But mobiles also offer specific tools not available on computers, and these can be used to good effect for publishers. Publishers can optimize their ads for mobile owners by making them easy to access by this audience. Publishers can also make good use of text and instant messaging to promote their offers. As the mobile market is predicted to make up 80% of traffic in the future, publishers who do not promote on mobile devices are missing out on a substantial opportunity.

    The best way to find affiliate publishers is on reputable networks like ShareASale Cj(Commission Junction), Awin, and Impact radius. These networks have a strict application process and compliance checks, which means that all affiliates are trustworthy.

    An affiliate disclosure statement discloses to the reader that there may be affiliate links on a website, for which a commission may be paid to the publisher if visitors follow these links and make purchases.

    Recent findings suggest that publishers promote their programs through a variety of means, including blogs, websites, email marketing, and pay-per-click ads. Social media has a huge interactive audience, making this platform a good source of potential traffic.

    A super affiliate is an affiliate partner who consistently drives a large majority of sales from any program they promote, compared to other affiliate partners involved in that program. Affiliates make a lot of money from affiliate marketing Pat Flynn earned more than $50000 in 2013 from affiliate marketing.

    Recent findings suggest that because the Internet is so widespread, affiliate programs can be promoted in any country. Affiliate strategies that are set internationally need to be tailored to the language of the targeted country.

    Affiliate marketing can help you grow your business in the following ways:.

    One of the best ways to work with qualified affiliates is to hire an affiliate marketing agency that works with all the networks. Affiliates are carefully selected and go through a rigorous application process to be included in the network.

    Affiliate marketing is generally associated with websites, but there are other ways to promote your affiliate links, including:.

    Industry observers note that commission rates are typically based on a percentage of the total sale and in some cases can also be a flat fee for each transaction. The rates are set by the merchant.

    Who manages your affiliate program?

    Some merchants run their affiliate programs internally, while others choose to contract out management to a network or an external agency.

    How to Run GLM-5.4 Locally (No Weights Yet, and It'll Be Slower Than GLM-5.3)

    📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1007 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dev

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • You can't run GLM-5.4 locally today.
    • It has been revealed that the line from the announcement that got quoted on HN is "We initiative to open-source the model weights responsibly after completing necessary safety hardening." No date is given.
    • Sources indicate that A normal transformer runs every layer once per token.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    You can't run GLM-5.4 locally today. Z.ai shipped it on November 23, 2026 as its first loop transformer coding model, and the weights aren't public yet. There's no Hugging Face repo, no model card and no license file. The zai-org org page still stops at GLM-5.3.

    It has been revealed that the line from the announcement that got quoted on HN is "We initiative to open-source the model weights responsibly after completing necessary safety hardening." No date is given. When the weights do land, the loop changes your hardware math in a way most "how much VRAM do I need" posts will get wrong. Below I work out a memory budget from GLM-5.3's numbers and check how far llama.cpp, vLLM, MLX and Ollama are from loading it.

    Sources indicate that A normal transformer runs every layer once per token. GLM-5.4 takes a block of 28 layers from the GLM-5 base and runs that block twice per token, using the same weights both times. WCCFtech, TestingCatalog and DataCamp all describe it the same way.

    Recent findings suggest that it wasn't trained looped from scratch. Z.ai took the already-pretrained GLM-5 base and converted the middle layers into a loop through continued training. GLM-5's config.json has "num_hidden_layers": 78. That's why one HN commenter summed it up as "emulating a 106 layer model in a 78 layer model.".

    According to DataCamp's write-up of the blog, there are two extra pieces that matter for anyone who will implement this in a runtime:.

    In this release the loop count is two, every token, every time. It doesn't loop until convergence, and it doesn't vary by token difficulty. Several HN commenters had to correct each other on that. Z.ai states it will keep scaling loop depth alongside model size, so later versions may differ.

    That last row is the one I have a problem with.

    In a recent development, Z.ai published no benchmark scores for GLM-5.4 itself, coding or otherwise. The only numbers come from a 30B iso-parameter ablation. With "about 10% more" training compute, the looped version beat the plain one, with the biggest gains on math, science reasoning and long context, and 10-14% shorter outputs on GPQA-Diamond and MMLU-Pro. The headline claim is that the ~750B model reaches intelligence comparable to 2T-3T parameter models. According to TestingCatalog, a Z.ai team member stated 5.4 scores will come later.

    For comparison, GLM-5.3's model card lists Terminal Bench 2.1 at 88.2, DeepSWE (v1.1) at 66.9 and NL2Repo at 58.0. That's the bar 5.4 has to clear, and Z.ai chose not to show whether it does.

    The only third-party number I found is AICodeKing's KingBench 4, via DataCamp: 7th overall and 1st among open models. It took 431 minutes against Gemini 4 Neon's 109, burned about 1.04M tokens against roughly 70,000, and had a 1.56% tool-call failure rate (11th of 17). DataCamp notes it's one reviewer's own harness, and people on X have already questioned which reasoning effort was used. So it's good, but it thinks a lot. Z.ai itself admits to "marathon thinking" loops.

    Early HN reports match that: "decent improvement on 5.3 but nothing earth shattering," "only marginally" better on one person's codebase, and one note that "it switches to Chinese at some point.".

    Sources indicate that my read: shipping a new architecture on a subscription plan, with no benchmark table and no weights, is a launch built for two news cycles. Maybe the numbers are fine. But "trust us, it matches a 3T model" from a 30B ablation is not evidence.

    Because the looped layers share weights, memory scales with physical parameters while compute scales with layer passes, so the two need separate estimates.

    Recent findings suggest that memory: the file size should land very close to GLM-5.3's. Treat these as estimates until a GGUF exists. Unsloth's GLM-5.3 guide lists the closest numbers available:.

    For datacenter hardware, vLLM's recipe indicates the FP8 GLM-5.3 checkpoint "fits on a single 8xH200 / 8xH20 node", and that reaching the full 1M context takes 8xB200 with FP8 KV cache. Add a little for GLM-5.4: the loop gates, a vision encoder, and a sliding-window KV for the second pass.

    Compute: every token now goes through roughly 106 layer passes instead of 78. That works out to about 36% more work per token from the layer count alone, even though the parameter count hasn't moved. Z.ai credits fused kernels with cutting the extra memory reads and writes the loop adds. On your hardware, expect it to be slower than GLM-5.3 at the same quant.

    Recent findings suggest that HN argued about whether looping helps the memory-bandwidth wall. The clearest answer came from user ac29: "Looping saves you memory capacity needs, not memory throughput needs." At batch size 1 on a Mac, you're still streaming the same expert weights, just more times.

    Recent findings suggest that none, because there's nothing to load. Where each one stands:.

    If you want GLM-5.4 now, it's on the GLM Coding Initiative, ZCode and Z.ai Chat. It's not on the regular API or OpenRouter yet. In Claude Code the model ID is glm-5.4[1m]. In OpenCode it's "model": "zai-coding-plan/glm-5.4".

    If you want local, run GLM-5.3 with Unsloth's commands. They should carry over almost unchanged once 5.4 quants exist:.

    To know when the weights drop, poll the HF API instead of refreshing Twitter:.

    Recent findings suggest that Z.ai has kept this promise before: GLM-5 and GLM-5.3 both ended up on Hugging Face, and as one HN commenter put it, "they usually take a few weeks to release the weights". The license has drifted, though. GLM-5 was MIT and GLM-5.3 ships under a custom glm-5.3 license, so read whatever 5.4 comes with before you build on it.

    In a recent development, A fixed two-pass loop on a ~750B MoE means more thinking per token at the same memory. Would you take slower tokens for that, or is a fast 27B Qwen still the better deal on your box? And what would GLM-5.4 have to beat, on which benchmark, for you to switch from Qwen?

    Recent findings suggest that when you’re limited to testing two variables against each other at a time, it can take months to get the results you’re looking for.     Acrolinx is a content alignment platform that helps brands scale and improves the quality of their content. It’s geared toward enterprises – its major customers include big brands like Google, Adobe, and Amazon - to help them scale their writing efforts. Instead of spending time chasing down and fixing typos in multiple places throughout an article or blog post, you can use Acrolinx to do it all right there in one place. You start by setting your preferences for style, grammar, tone of voice, and manufacturer-specific word usage. Then, Acrolinx checks and scores your existing content to find what’s working and suggest areas for improvement. The platform provides real-time guidance and suggestions to make writing better and strengthen weak pages.

    In a recent development, marketMuse uses an algorithm to help marketers build content strategies. The tool demonstrates you where to target keywords to rank in specific topic categories, and recommends keywords you should go after if you want to own particular topics. It also identifies gaps and opportunities for newly introduced content and prioritizes them by their probable impact on your rankings. The algorithm compares your content with thousands of articles related to the same topic to uncover what’s missing from your site.

    Industry observers note that copilot is a suite of tools that help eCommerce businesses maintain real-time communication with customers around the clock at every stage of the funnel. Promote products, recover shopping carts and send updates or reminders directly through Messenger.

    Yotpo’s deep learning technology evaluates your customers’ product reviews to help you make better business decisions. It identifies key topics that customers mention related to your products—and their feelings toward them. The AI engine extracts relevant reviews from past buyers and presents them in smart displays to convert newly introduced shoppers. Yotpo also saves you time moderating reviews. The AI-powered moderation tool automatically assigns a score to each review and flags reviews with negative sentiment so you can focus on quality control instead of manually reviewing every post.

    In a recent development, albert is a self-learning software that automates the creation of marketing campaigns for your brand. It analyzes vast amounts of data to run optimized campaigns autonomously, allowing you to feed in your own creative content and target markets, and then use data from its database to determine key characteristics of a serious buyer. Albert identifies potential customers that match those traits, and runs trial campaigns on a small group of customers—with results refined by Albert himself—before launching it on a larger scale.

    Albert plugs into your existing marketing technology stack, so you still have access to your accounts, ads, search, social media, and more. Albert maps tracking and attribution to your source of truth so you can determine which channels are driving your business.

    There are many tools and companies out there that offer AI tools, but this is a small list of resources that we have found to be helpful. As marketing evolves at such a rapid pace, new marketing strategies will be invented that we haven't even dreamed of yet.     #183764. Controlling Generated Code with Git, Diffs, and Tests

    📅 24 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 2m • 📖 Standard (401 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Dev ↗ Open Full Page

    Controlling Generated Code with Git, Diffs, and Tests

    📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (401 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Dev

    ⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • According to recent reports, working with AI-generated code can feel like magic—until it isn’t.
    • Here are four practical insights to keep AI-generated code under control:.
    • Trust the diff, not the story A PR description that notes “everything is done” is not proof.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    According to recent reports, working with AI-generated code can feel like magic—until it isn’t. The speed at which tools like Claude Code or Codex produce working code is impressive, but trusting the narrative without inspecting the concrete changes is a shortcut to technical debt. Git diffs and tests aren’t just overhead; they’re your control panel for understanding what actually happened, what was verified, and where things might break tomorrow.

    Here are four practical insights to keep AI-generated code under control:.

    Trust the diff, not the story A PR description that notes “everything is done” is not proof. The real evidence lives in the diff: which files changed, what dependencies were added, and how the behavior was validated. Without reviewing the actual changes, you risk trusting a compelling narrative instead of verifying the work. Start every review with git status and git diff to ground your understanding in facts, not assumptions.

    Plan before you code Before letting an AI modify files, ask for a concrete plan: which files will change, what tests will be added, and how you’ll validate the result. This turns the final diff into a verifiable artifact rather than an opaque block of code. For example, when adding a CPU chart, insist on a focused plan—display logic, error handling, and tests—before any file is touched.

    It has been revealed that small commits are reasoning units A large diff that includes multiple features, abstractions, and fixes may work, but it’s nearly impossible to review. Breaking work into small, intentional commits—like adding one chart, handling one error case, then testing—lets you verify each step and roll back safely if something breaks. Each commit should tell a clear story, not recount your entire day.

    Tests should protect needs, not just code A passing test only confirms that the code behaves as written, not that it protects a useful behavior. Before writing tests, describe the expected behavior in plain language: valid values, edge cases, missing data, and error states. Then let the AI help refine the test suite—but don’t let it define the strategy. Intentionally break the behavior you think is protected to see if the test actually catches it.

    Sources indicate that you don’t need to slow down to stay in control. You need to know where to look, what to verify, and when to say no. That’s how AI becomes a force multiplier—not a black box.

    https://nicolas-dabene.fr/en/blog/controlling-generated-code-with-git-diffs-and-tests/.
